# Test

Unit tests: checks with readable failures, and the runner that #Test() functions are gathered into.

## Installation

Add `Test` to the `[Dependencies]` table of your package's `Rux.toml`:

```toml
[Dependencies]
Test = { Namespace = "Rux", Version = "0.1.0" }
```

Standard packages are declared by hand: the registry does not serve them, so `rux add Rux/Test` cannot add them.

## Dependencies

- [`Allocator`](/docs/api/allocator) 0.1.0
- [`Collections`](/docs/api/collections) 0.1.0
- [`Core`](/docs/api/core) 0.1.0
- [`Format`](/docs/api/format) 0.1.0
- [`Io`](/docs/api/io) 0.1.0
- [`Process`](/docs/api/process) 0.1.0

- [`Time`](/docs/api/time) 0.1.0

## Guide

Unit tests: functions marked `#Test()`, checks whose failures say what was expected and what was found, and the runner a test build gathers them into.

### What it provides

| Module                                   | Covers                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| [`Expect`](/docs/api/test/expect#expect) | [`Expect`](/docs/api/test/expect#expect), [`ExpectEqual`](/docs/api/test/expect#expect-equal), [`ExpectNotEqual`](/docs/api/test/expect#expect-not-equal), [`ExpectNear`](/docs/api/test/expect#expect-near), [`ExpectText`](/docs/api/test/expect#expect-text), [`ExpectSome`](/docs/api/test/expect#expect-some), [`ExpectNone`](/docs/api/test/expect#expect-none), [`ExpectSuccess`](/docs/api/test/expect#expect-success) and [`ExpectFailure`](/docs/api/test/expect#expect-failure) |
| `Failure`                                | [`TestFailure`](/docs/api/test/failure#test-failure), a failure with its message or a skip with its reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `Runner`                                 | [`TestCase`](/docs/api/test/runner#test-case), [`TestOptions`](/docs/api/test/runner#test-options), [`RunTests`](/docs/api/test/runner#run-tests), which reads its filters from the command line, and [`RunTestsWith`](/docs/api/test/runner#run-tests-with)                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `Benchmark`                              | [`BenchmarkCase`](/docs/api/test/benchmark#benchmark-case), [`BenchmarkOptions`](/docs/api/test/benchmark#benchmark-options), [`BenchmarkResult`](/docs/api/test/benchmark#benchmark-result), [`Measure`](/docs/api/test/benchmark#measure), [`Consume`](/docs/api/test/benchmark#consume), [`RunBenchmarks`](/docs/api/test/benchmark#run-benchmarks) and [`RunBenchmarksWith`](/docs/api/test/benchmark#run-benchmarks-with)                                                             |

The module names describe where each declaration comes from; they are not part of an import path.

### Example

```rux
import Test::{ ExpectEqual, ExpectText, TestFailure };

func Greeting(name: char8[..]) -> char8[..] {
    return name.length == 0 ? "hello" : "hello, friend";
}

#Test()
func GreetsAnyone() -> ! TestFailure {
    ExpectText(Greeting(""), "hello")?;
    ExpectEqual(Greeting("ann").length, 13u)?;
}
```

`rux test` builds the package in test mode and runs it, reporting each test with its time, and `rux test -- Greets` runs only the tests whose names hold `Greets`.

### Design

A test is a function marked `#Test()` that takes nothing and returns nothing or `! TestFailure`. It is declared at the top level of a source file or inside a `module` block, which then prefixes its name, as in `Parser::ReadsNumbers`. Each check returns `! TestFailure`, so a test passes a failed check on with `?` and stops there. The failure says what was expected and what was found: [`ExpectText`](/docs/api/test/expect#expect-text) names the byte where two texts part and shows each around it. A test ends with `fail TestFailure::Skip("reason")` to be counted as skipped rather than failed. A failure keeps its message inline, so failing never allocates and never fails itself.

A test build of a package with `#Test()` functions generates its `Main`: a table of [`TestCase`](/docs/api/test/runner#test-case) values handed to [`RunTests`](/docs/api/test/runner#run-tests). This works for libraries too, so a `SourceLibrary` can hold its own tests beside its code. The package must depend on `Test` and must not declare a `Main` of its own. `rux test` runs every executable package under `Tests/` and every package whose sources mark tests, and passes the arguments after `--` to each. The runner reads a plain argument as a filter on test names, with `--exact` to match whole names, `--skip <text>` to leave some out, `--list` to list them and `--quiet` to report only failures.

A benchmark is a [`BenchmarkCase`](/docs/api/test/benchmark#benchmark-case): a name and a function that repeats the measured work as many times as it is told, so setup before its loop is not counted. [`Measure`](/docs/api/test/benchmark#measure) runs it with a count that grows from one, at least twofold and at most a hundredfold a round, aiming past the minimum time from the rate so far, until a run lasts 200 milliseconds or reaches its cap, and reports that run; [`RunBenchmarks`](/docs/api/test/benchmark#run-benchmarks) measures a table of them and prints the time per iteration of each, with a name filter and `--quick` from the command line. `Consume(@result)` keeps a result the compiler would otherwise see as unused, and the work that made it, from being optimized away.

Tests run one after another in one process. A failed check ends only its own test. A panic or a failed `Assert` ends the whole run, which `rux test` then reports with the output up to that point.

## Index

### Types

| Name                                                             | Summary                                                                                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`BenchmarkCase`](/docs/api/test/benchmark#benchmark-case)       | A benchmark: its name, which the runner reports and filters on, and the function that repeats the measured work as many times as it is told. |
| [`BenchmarkResult`](/docs/api/test/benchmark#benchmark-result)   | What a measurement found: how many iterations its final run made and how long that run took.                                                 |
| [`BenchmarkOptions`](/docs/api/test/benchmark#benchmark-options) | Which benchmarks a run chooses and how long each is measured.                                                                                |
| [`TestFailure`](/docs/api/test/failure#test-failure)             | Why a test did not pass.                                                                                                                     |
| [`TestCase`](/docs/api/test/runner#test-case)                    | A test: its name, which the runner reports and filters on, and the function that runs it.                                                    |
| [`TestOptions`](/docs/api/test/runner#test-options)              | Which tests a run chooses and how it reports them.                                                                                           |

### Functions

| Name                                                                | Summary                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`Consume<T>`](/docs/api/test/benchmark#consume)                    | Marks `value` as used, so the work that computed it is not removed as having no effect.                                                                                             |
| [`Measure`](/docs/api/test/benchmark#measure)                       | Runs `run` with a growing iteration count until one run lasts at least `options.minimumTime` or reaches `options.maximumIterations`, and reports that run.                          |
| [`RunBenchmarksWith`](/docs/api/test/benchmark#run-benchmarks-with) | Measures the benchmarks that `options` choose, in order, and reports each as its time per iteration and the iterations it was measured over, then how many were measured.           |
| [`RunBenchmarks`](/docs/api/test/benchmark#run-benchmarks)          | Measures the benchmarks the process's arguments choose.                                                                                                                             |
| [`Expect`](/docs/api/test/expect#expect)                            | Fails unless `condition` holds.                                                                                                                                                     |
| [`ExpectEqual<T>`](/docs/api/test/expect#expect-equal)              | Fails unless `actual` equals `expected`, saying both.                                                                                                                               |
| [`ExpectNotEqual<T>`](/docs/api/test/expect#expect-not-equal)       | Fails if `actual` equals `unexpected`.                                                                                                                                              |
| [`ExpectNear`](/docs/api/test/expect#expect-near)                   | Fails unless `actual` is within `tolerance` of `expected`.                                                                                                                          |
| [`ExpectText`](/docs/api/test/expect#expect-text)                   | Fails unless `actual` is the same text as `expected`, saying at which byte they part and showing each around it.                                                                    |
| [`ExpectSome<T>`](/docs/api/test/expect#expect-some)                | The value of `value`, failing when there is none.                                                                                                                                   |
| [`ExpectNone<T>`](/docs/api/test/expect#expect-none)                | Fails when `value` is present.                                                                                                                                                      |
| [`ExpectSuccess<T, E>`](/docs/api/test/expect#expect-success)       | The success of `outcome`, failing when it failed.                                                                                                                                   |
| [`ExpectFailure<T, E>`](/docs/api/test/expect#expect-failure)       | The failure of `outcome`, failing the test when it succeeded.                                                                                                                       |
| [`RunTestsWith`](/docs/api/test/runner#run-tests-with)              | Runs the tests that `options` choose, in order, and reports each as `ok`, `FAILED` with its message, or `skipped` with its reason, then a summary of the counts and the time taken. |
| [`RunTests`](/docs/api/test/runner#run-tests)                       | Runs the tests the process's arguments choose.                                                                                                                                      |
